reasons: Directionally correct: Section 2.2 imposes a full-term sole-supplier obligation on Customer with no category limit, time limit, or performance exit — the rule's walk-away position — so 'deviation' is the right status.

The redline reaches the preferred position by converting Vendor to a non-exclusive provider and expressly preserving our right to source from third parties; no residual requirements/exclusivity obligation on Customer remains, and no exclusivity running in Customer's favour was removed.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.650 changed-character ratio) is not disqualifying here: the clause is a single short sentence whose entire operative content is the exclusivity grant, so removing it necessarily rewrites most of the text. The added third-party procurement right is a reasonable, narrow confirmation consistent with Section 12.3.

Comment is accurate and correctly scoped: it states what changed, cites the playbook prohibition, flags the Section 12.3 conflict, and offers the fallback (single category, 12 months, automatic termination on SLA/delivery failure) without lecturing; tone and prefix conform.
